references.text: The parents present the evidence of virginity in response to the man's false accusations that he did not find signs of virginity in her.
The penalty for a man who falsely accuses his wife of not having been a virgin: he must pay one hundred shekels of silver and can never divorce her.
Prohibition against spreading false rumors, which is relevant to the man's evil slander of his wife.
Prohibition against going about with gossip among the people, related to spreading a bad report about one's wife.
He who finds a wife finds happiness - in contrast to the man who falsely accuses his wife.
A false witness who spreads lies is something the Lord hates, relevant to the man's false accusations.
